verses.1: And there was a man from Ramathaim, who lived in Ephraim. His name was Elkanah, son of Jeroham, son of Elihu, son of Tochobaz, son of Zuph.
verses.2: And there were two women. One woman’s name was Hanah, and the other woman’s name was Penina. Penina had children, but Hanah did not have any children.
verses.3: And that man went up from his city since ancient times, to worship and offer sacrifices to the Lord’s angels in the temple. There were also two priests of Eliezer and Pinchas who served as priests to the Lord.
verses.4: And that day came, and Elkanah offered sacrifices. He gave his wife and all his daughters and daughters-in-law offerings.
verses.5: And He will give her one lamb, because He loves her. And Jehovah will protect her.
verses.6: And because of her anger, she also suffered harm due to her wrath. For Jehovah closed in upon her with His mercy.
verses.7: And so, each year, she will be taken up into the house of Jehovah. In that time, she will be angry and cry, and she will not eat.
verses.8: And Elkanah said to her, “Why should you mourn? Why shouldn’t you eat? And why should you be sad? I am good for you, with twelve sons.”
verses.9: And Hanan rose up after eating, and after drinking. And above him sat the priest, on the throne of Jehovah’s house.
verses.10: And she became very sad and prayed to Jehovah. She wept bitterly.
verses.11: And Nadar said, “Lord, your army! If you see this, then remember me. Do not forget your promise to me. You have given me the seed of men, and you have placed it under Jehovah’s care for their entire lives. No evil shall ever come upon them.”
verses.12: And it shall be that she would pray more and more before Jehovah, and she would keep her mouth shut.
verses.13: And Chanah spoke to her heart, but her lips moved, and her voice could not be heard. She thought of herself as being worthy of being hired out.
verses.14: And he said to her, “Until my death, you shall be covered with dirt; your face shall remain covered from sight.”
verses.15: And Hannah cried out, “No, my Lord! I am a woman with a heavy heart. I have not received any reward from You. I will throw myself before the face of the LORD.”
verses.16: Do not give your truth to a girl who is not worthy of it. For my words have been too many and my anger has been too great until now.
verses.17: And he stood up and said to her, “May the Lord of Israel give you back your son whom you asked of him.”
verses.18: And it was said, “Find grace in your eyes for your wife.” Then the woman went on her way, ate, and her face was no longer sad.
verses.19: And they rested in the evening. They bowed down before Jehovah. Then they returned to their homes. Elkanah knew about his wife’s pregnancy. And Jehovah remembered him.
verses.20: And during those days, Hannah became pregnant and gave birth to a son. She named him Shemuel, because it was from Jehovah that she received this name.
verses.21: And the man went up to Elkanah and all his household, to offer to the LORD the offerings that were required on those days, as well as the incense.
verses.22: And Hannah did not go, because she said to her sister-in-law, “Wait until the boy is circumcised and brought back. Then we will see the face of Jehovah, and he will sit there forever.”
verses.23: And Elkanah said to her, “Do what is good in my eyes. Let me keep your son until you can see him again. But God will carry out His word.” Then the woman stayed and nursed her son until he grew up.
verses.24: And she carried them with her, as they were wrapped in three bundles of cloth. One bundle was broken, and the boy came into the house of Jehovah. The boy was still a child at that time.
verses.25: And they slaughtered the sheep, and brought the young boy to the top.
verses.26: And my Lord said, “Live on, my soul! My Lord, I am the woman who stands with you here, in order to pray to Jehovah.”
verses.27: To this young man, I prayed. And Jehovah granted me what I asked of Him.
verses.28: And I also asked Him to do this for Jehovah, all the days that He was a priest to Jehovah. He bowed down there before Jehovah.
